clue.text: Officer's quarter attached to a former prison

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking officer, here with a possessive S
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An officer's lodgings have been built onto an old jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was a notorious debtors' prison in Southwark, London, closed in 1842. 'a' gives its own letter and 'attached to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name of a historic London debtors' jail, demolished in the nineteenth century.

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
to revile is to abuse

explanation.surface: Lots of people speak ill of an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jan Mabuse (Gossaert) was a sixteenth-century Flemish painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Byname of the Flemish Renaissance artist Jan Gossaert.

indicators.note: capital means the head letter, so the first letter of Rome's is taken

parts.note: Odin is the chief Norse god

explanation.surface: A sculptor who carved the god at the head of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Rome as capital city; it takes the first letter of 'Rome's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste, the French artist who made The Thinker and The Kiss.

parts.note: Thomas Hood was an English poet
forty winks is a nap, so one of them is a wink

explanation.surface: A question whether a deceiving poet is one of the Forty Thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty winks is a short sleep, so 'one of forty' is a wink. Thomas Hood wrote The Song of the Shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to trick or fool someone.

explanation.surface: A scientist may have a spare room to let.
explanation.walkthrough: To lodge is to stay in rented rooms; Sir Oliver Lodge was a British physicist and radio pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to stay as a lodger in someone's house; Sir Oliver Lodge was an English physicist.

clue.text: Medium output from Tom's place, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of Tom's place may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A medium's spooky product turning up at Tom's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TOMSPLACE. 'Medium' is a spiritualist, not a size; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The ghostly substance said to flow from a spiritualist in a seance.

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words shop, usually

explanation.surface: Someone describes their usual job behind a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters running across 'shOP USually'.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition is numbered as a work in a composer's catalogue.

clue.text: Detectives in Francois' homeland discover a crime

indicators.note: in places the detectives inside the French word for homeland

parts.note: patrie is French for homeland
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police officers in France uncover a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CID inside PATRIE, the French for fatherland; 'discover a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The killing of one's own father, a grave offence.

parts.note: not lines of verse by the poet Browning but rays that brown the skin

explanation.surface: A reference to verse by the poet Robert Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' looks like the Victorian poet; here it means tanning, and the lines are rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays from the sun, which tan the skin.

explanation.surface: Something growing in Germany's Black Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Forest' reads as the German region; split it into 'Black' (the colour) and 'Forest growth' (the tree).
explanation.definitionFit: A deep dark colour, and the hard dark tropical tree that gives its name.

clue.text: Once the cheapest resting place in town!

definitions.text: Once the cheapest resting place in town!

parts.words: Once the cheapest resting place in town!
parts.note: a bed for a penny, D being the old pre-decimal penny, gives the name of an English county town

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain lodging used to be the cheapest in town.
explanation.walkthrough: D was the abbreviation for the old British penny, so a bed for a penny was 'once the cheapest resting place'; split that way it is the county town of Bedfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An English county town north of London, which split up reads as a bed costing an old penny.

clue.text: Asian language can include a Greek letter

indicators.note: include tells us one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A claim that a tin can contain a Greek character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts BETA inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken on the high plateau north of the Himalayas, around Lhasa.

indicators.note: varied means changed in form, so the letters of the word wines are rearranged

explanation.surface: Different wines vary in their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges the letters of WINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical power or muscle, as in the sinews of war.

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer
the answer to 2 down sculpted The Thinker, whose model sits deep in thought, that is, pensive

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sitter has stopped resembling a sculptor's model.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down's most famous statue is The Thinker, a pensive figure; someone no longer like him is ex-pensive. The definition 'dear' means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly, high-priced.

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher hears a call in a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Hatton Garden is London's diamond and jewellery quarter, so the talk heard there is stone chat. The stonechat is a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird named for its call like pebbles knocked together; in the jewellers' quarter the dealers' talk is about gems.

indicators.note: disturbance means upheaval, so the letters of can settle are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: People ask whether calm can be restored after unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges CANSETTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelers of an octopus or snail, the organs with which these creatures touch.

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone reflects but finds nothing peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges DISCERNS with O; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponders or reflects upon.

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the word for the post is read from end to start

parts.note: the post is the mail

explanation.surface: An Irishman sends back the letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MAIL round.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Irish boy's name, a short form of William.

clue.text: Furnace-man is retired — has gone for trip

parts.note: retired to bed, so abed

indicators.note: gone for a trip means the letters of gone have tripped and fallen into a new order

explanation.surface: A stoker has gone to bed after being on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Abednego, with Shadrach and Meshach, was thrown into Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace in the Book of Daniel. 'for trip' rearranges GONE; 'is' and 'has' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical figure who survived the burning fiery furnace.

clue.text: Workers have afterthought about old furniture

indicators.note: about means around, so the postscript goes round the old furniture

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought in a letter
lumber is disused old furniture

explanation.surface: Some workmen add a note about antique chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LUMBER inside PS; 'have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen who fit pipes and water systems.

parts.note: read not as the sea floor but as a bed on board an ocean-going ship

explanation.surface: The floor of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ocean bed' suggests the seabed, but it is a sleeping berth on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow shelf-like berth for sleeping on a ship.

clue.text: East called about length to be given a coating

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for called goes round the unit of length

parts.note: called means named
an ell is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A person from the east is said to be getting a covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ELL, an old measure of cloth, inside NAMED, after E. 'to be' joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered with a glossy glaze or paint, as pottery or metal is.

clue.text: N. Nickleby's uncle ran in Xanadu

parts.note: R stands for river, the river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan
Alph is the sacred river that ran in Xanadu in Coleridge's poem

explanation.surface: Nicholas Nickleby's uncle went running in a fabled city.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan: 'In Xanadu ... where Alph, the sacred river, ran'. So the phrase describes R (river) ALPH. Ralph Nickleby is the villainous uncle in Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of the miserly moneylender uncle in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.

parts.note: not a tall person but a creature standing on six legs

explanation.surface: A person taller than six feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over six feet' suggests height; it means a creature that stands on six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug, which has three pairs of legs.

parts.note: not a football official but one who supplies the lines spoken in a stage play

explanation.surface: A football linesman is asked to take part in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' looks like the sports official; here it is the person who writes the actors' lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright, who writes the speeches for the theatre.

parts.note: a type is a kind or version
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about the fifth draft of a Melville book.
explanation.walkthrough: Types lettered A, B, C... would make type E the fifth version. Typee was Herman Melville's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Title of Herman Melville's 1846 South Seas novel.

explanation.surface: A socialite who also writes fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Society' is the secret society of Freemasons; the novelist is A. E. W. Mason, author of The Four Feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason is a member of a fraternal society; A. E. W. Mason wrote adventure fiction.

explanation.surface: A sort of military headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAPE was Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, NATO's command; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shape is a form or outline; SHAPE is NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe.

clue.text: Fifty pieces of mash for racehorse

indicators.note: mash means crush into a pulp, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A recipe for a stable feed: fifty bits of bran mash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mash' (with 'of' as link) rearranges L and PIECES. Eclipse was an unbeaten eighteenth-century English racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of a famous unbeaten English racer of the 1760s.

clue.text: Talk foolishly about the Spanish ecclesiastic

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for talking foolishly goes round the Spanish article

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone babbles about the Spanish clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EL inside PRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or other senior churchman.

clue.text: Expel from a country in the Old Testament

indicators.note: in places the country inside the abbreviation for the scripture

parts.note: OT is the abbreviation for the Old Testament
US, the United States, is a country

explanation.surface: Someone is banished from a land in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a country in the Old Testament' looks like a Bible land; 'in' puts US inside OT, and 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive out or remove someone from a position.

clue.text: Tax fools people, in a way

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: in puts the word for people inside the abbreviation for a street

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
men are people

explanation.surface: A levy that, in a sense, makes fools of the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MEN inside ST (street), after ASSES; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a levy or rate fixed on property or income.
